annotation.kind: source-faithful Cholesky-coordinate and finite-sequence formalization of all five parts of Proposition 6.2

assumptions: The represented matrices are symmetric positive definite and have positive-diagonal lower Cholesky factors.
The formal dimension is n+1: lambdaMin is one eigenvalue and tailEigen contains the remaining n positive eigenvalues.
The supplied determinant, diagonal-product, eigenvalue-product, trace, and exact Jacobi-step identities are the coordinate identities used explicitly in the paper's proof.
The finite natural number M selects an arbitrary finite prefix of the exact Jacobi sequence; no floating-point effects are modeled in Proposition 6.2.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P35 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P35 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p35_t3_hadamard_measure_jacobi_growth (n M L s detH diagProduct measure jacobiEntry lambdaMin lambdaMax tailEigen kappa) ... : the five Hadamard-measure and Jacobi-growth conclusions
formal_statement.plain_language: The Hadamard measure has the upper bound and diagonal equality case, is invariant under diagonal scaling, controls the smallest normalized eigenvalue, increases at every exact Jacobi step by the stated factor, and bounds condition growth throughout a finite Jacobi run.

informal_proof: Use the Cholesky row-energy and determinant products for the first two parts. Apply finite AM-GM to the n tail eigenvalues and the standard binomial bound by exp(1) for the third. Use determinant preservation and the exact diagonal-product update for the fourth, then induct over the Jacobi steps and combine the smallest- and largest-eigenvalue bounds for the fifth.
informal_statement: Proposition 6.2: prove all five properties of the Hadamard measure, including its equality case, diagonal-scaling invariance, normalized smallest-eigenvalue bound, exact Jacobi-step increase, and global condition-growth bound.

tier_rationale: The task retains all five parts of Proposition 6.2. Its proof must establish equality in a dimension-indexed Cholesky product inequality, diagonal-scale cancellation, a general finite AM-GM and exponential estimate, exact Jacobi-step monotonicity, and an induction producing the global condition-number bound. This is at least T2-level effort and is not discharged by a Mathlib import. NumStability has no corresponding compiled Hadamard-measure or exact Jacobi-growth result, so L receives no material advantage over N.
